query: what is vicarious trauma and how can it be coped with?
generator_output: Vicarious trauma is a type of trauma that occurs when a person experiences emotional distress and symptoms similar to those of a trauma survivor, without having directly experienced the traumatic event. This can happen to people who work closely with trauma survivors, such as healthcare professionals, counselors, social workers, and first responders.  Symptoms of vicarious trauma can include feelings of anxiety, depression, anger, guilt, and a sense of helplessness. Some people may also experience physical symptoms such as headaches, stomachaches, and difficulty sleeping. In severe cases, vicarious trauma can lead to burnout, compassion fatigue, and even post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).  To cope with vicarious trauma, it is important to take care of oneself and seek support from others. Gap in Coverage: Many employers only offer short-term disability insurance, which may not be enough to cover
